**What the pinned code supports**

The PATH_INFO protection present in the tree is the guard in `config_defaults_inc.php:219-240` (sanitize `SCRIPT_NAME`, reject `&#`). It only covers the `$g_path` derivation. Real, independent reflections remain:

| Trap | Site | Mechanism | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | `core/filter_form_api.php:2396` → `:2434` (raw `PHP_SELF` in filter-link href; callers `view_filters_page.php:143`, `manage_filter_edit_page.php:137`) | M4, advisory route | absent |
| T2 | `core/timeline_inc.php:49` → `:91/:98/:119` (`string_sanitize_url()` leaves quotes/spaces in the script path, then href echoed raw) | M8, weak check | weak |
| T3 | `admin/email_queue.php:159` (raw `SCRIPT_NAME` in form action, admin-only) | M4 | absent |
| T4 | `config_defaults_inc.php:202-211,250` → `core/session_api.php:221` (check covers `$t_path` but not `$t_host` in `$g_path`) | M10 | weak |

T2 is the interesting one: the code already calls `string_sanitize_url(basename(SCRIPT_NAME))`, which `strip_tags`/`urldecode`s but re-emits the URL "script" component with only backslashes encoded (`string_api.php:280,315`) — so a quote survives into the `<a href="...">`. T1 is the classic `PHP_SELF`/PATH_INFO vector and the likely reported route.

**Verdict:** usable. Recommended stack T1 + T2 + T3 (different fix sites, different dismiss reasons: reported route; "sanitizer already applied"; admin-only/other directory), with T2 (`mimo`, how-type) and T3 (`deepseek`, absent + dismiss) covering both model profiles. T4 is real but host-header-dependent and excluded from the design.
